BREAKING: Tesla is making a strong comeback across Europe. 🇪🇺

• Registrations across the EU, UK, and EFTA surged more than 50% year over year in June, exceeding 51,000 vehicles.
• The Model Y led the market with 34,050 registrations, up 37.9%.
• Model Y was Europe's best-selling vehicle in June, beating every EV, hybrid, and gas car.
• It outsold the second-place Dacia Sandero by nearly 8,600 units.

First-half 2026 highlights:
• Tesla registrations reached around 170,000.
• Model Y sales climbed 59% year over year.
• Model Y ranked as Europe's No. 2 best-selling vehicle in H1, fewer than 2,500 registrations behind the Dacia Sandero.

The refreshed Model Y isn't just leading the EV market—it is now competing to become Europe's best-selling vehicle of 2026.

ELON SHUTS DOWN THE “DOGE KILLED PEOPLE” NARRATIVE

In the Economist interview, the editor pushed the claim that DOGE cuts to USAID caused deaths.

Elon’s response was direct:
“Zero.”

When pressed further, he said the claims are “false… nonsense and absolute nonsense.”
He pointed out that legitimate programs were moved to the State Department, and that when you stop funding fraudulent or ineffective organizations, the people who lost the money never admit it was waste — they invent the most sympathetic story possible to get the funding restored.
That’s exactly what happened.
The media ran with the emotional narrative. Elon stuck to the facts.

Video

. @elonmusk DESTROYS THE “FAR RIGHT” SMEAR
In the Economist interview, the editor tried the usual line:

“You support the far right…”

Elon’s response was perfect:

“No, I support the normal people. What you call the far right, falsely.”
He then listed three basic positions:
•  Secure borders
•  Safe cities
•  Sensible spending
And asked: “Which of those three are far right fringe?”
He went further:
“I would like to just admonish you and the media for the absurd characterization of the far right. It is false and misleading and nonsense.”
That’s the entire game right there. Take completely mainstream positions that were normal 10–15 years ago, rebrand them as “far right,” and then act shocked when people push back.
Elon refused to play along. He called it what it is — a dishonest framing designed to shut down debate.
The more the media overuses these labels, the less power they have.

ELON ON AI ACCELERATION

“If you can’t beat them, join them.”

Elon says every attempt he made to slow AI progress actually ended up accelerating it. His conclusion: all roads lead to acceleration.

The only realistic option left is to minimize the probability of a bad outcome — not pretend we can stop the train.

That’s why he founded xAI, and why he’s now pushing for rival AI labs to review each other’s models before release.
The race is on. The question is whether we steer it wisely.

LEGACY MEDIA TRIED TO SMEAR ELON AGAIN — AND HE SHUT IT DOWN

In the Economist interview, the editor went straight to the usual playbook:
“People say that you’re a racist.”

Elon’s response was simple and factual:
“My partner is half Indian, and I have four children with her. One of them was named after a famous Indian physicist. So I would say I’m not racist. And also, if you look at the people that are employed at my companies, we have senior executives of all races. I don’t think there’s any racism there.”

Then came the follow-up:

“Are you anti-Muslim?”

Elon:

“If people are coming to a country with antithetical views, I am against that. I’m against rape and murder. I’m against the imposition of rules and laws that are contrary to what we’ve come to accept in the West.”

That’s it. No hate. No racism. Just a clear distinction between people and values.
Yet legacy media still runs with the same tired narrative because it fits their script. They don’t want the nuance — they want the smear.

Elon keeps pointing out the obvious: 

opposing certain cultural values that clash with Western norms is not the same as hating an entire group of people. The media refuses to acknowledge the difference.
The more they push these accusations, the more transparent their bias becomes.

ELON JUST EXPOSED LEGACY MEDIA AGAIN

In the latest Economist interview, the editor-in-chief tried the usual line:
“People loathe you.”

Elon’s response was perfect:

“More people like me than don’t. Far more people hate you and the media than you realise.”

That’s the quiet part out loud.

Legacy media has spent years pushing distorted narratives, selective outrage, and outright misrepresentations about Elon — and it’s not working the way they think it is.
People see through it. 

The constant framing, the loaded questions, the attempt to turn every achievement into a threat… it’s gotten so predictable it’s almost comical.

Elon didn’t need a long speech. 

He just pointed out the obvious: the public’s trust in legacy media is collapsing, and they still act like they hold the moral high ground.

The more they attack him, the more transparent their bias becomes.

•  Sustainable energy

Fear the stagnation, not the acceleration.
